title: The Image of God
lead: Genesis says that God made humans "in our image, as our likeness" (1:26–27). The idea grounds human dignity and the ban on murder (9:6), shapes how the New Testament speaks of Christ as the image of God (Colossians 1:15), and of believers being renewed into that image (2 Corinthians 3:18).

sections.b:
The phrase appears only three times in the Old Testament (Genesis 1:26–27; 5:1–3; 9:6), but Psalm 8 sings the same idea: God made humans "a little lower than God" and put all things under their feet. James 3:9 forbids cursing people who are made in God's likeness. Paul calls Christ "the image of the invisible God" (Colossians 1:15; 2 Corinthians 4:4) and says believers are being changed into his image (Romans 8:29; 2 Corinthians 3:18; Colossians 3:10).

Interpreters have located the image in reason and the soul (much of classic theology), in relationship and love (Karl Barth, stressing "male and female"), or in a royal task: humans stand for God on earth, as a statue stood for a king (D. J. A. Clines; J. Richard Middleton). Many combine these.
